text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ports authority and state oil firm NNPC resolve dispute over handling charges that led to shortage of aviation fuel and grounding of domestic flights nationwide.

- Federal Appeal Court in capital Abuja rules that detained presidential claimant Moshood Abiola does not need to be brought to court to name which of two contending lawyers should represent him in his treason trial.
- Defence headquarters confirms that 22 unnamed suspects have been arrested over recent spate of bombings in Lagos.
- Nigerian government adopts policy of balanced budgeting as huge surplus from last year covers deficit in projected spending for 1997.

- Cross section of business operators fault government's decision to delay privatisation of state enterprises but others say it is wise for government to do its homework properly before proceeding with the policy.
- Lagos state budgets 12.8 billion naira for 1997.

- Bankers say mergers imminent in banking sector following government order that banks should raise their capital base to 500 million naira by end-March from 50 million or be liquidated. Guardian calculates that banks need 7.34 billion naira to comply with new policy.
- Some past and present officials of the Central Bank may be arraigned before failed banks tribunal for allegedly contributing to distress of some banks, official sources say.
- Petroleum Trust Fund, which is charged with spending some of the money made from higher pump prices, may import rice to further push down the price of the staple, official sources say.
- Nigeria's anti-narcotics chief Major-General Musa Bamaiyi urges United States to support Nigeria's fight against drugs.
